attacks.claim: S6's export-count check is unexecutable: it runs `node -e "import('./packages/core/dist/index.js')"` after `pnpm build`, but packages/core's build script is `tsc --noEmit` and its exports field is `".": "./src/index.ts"` — no dist/index.js exists on disk or is ever produced, so the command fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and the claimed 'expected delta is exactly -1' can never be measured as written.
attacks.evidence: packages/core/package.json lines 6-8 (`"exports": { ".": "./src/index.ts" }`) and line 15 (`"build": "tsc --noEmit"`); `ls packages/core/dist` returns nothing at HEAD.
attacks.repair: Replace the dist import with something the workspace can actually run: either (a) a throwaway vitest spec in packages/core that does `import * as m from '../index'` and asserts `Object.keys(m)` / `Object.keys(m.voice)` deltas (vitest already executes TS there), or (b) drop the runtime count entirely and let the knip before/after diff plus `rg -n '^export' packages/core/src/index.ts` carry the interface-delta evidence. Do not add a build step to core for this.

attacks.claim: S1's dynamic-access proofs are mangled regexes that vacuously match nothing, so the step's ABORT gate cannot fire even if bracket access existed: the pattern `\['\"\`](...)` escapes the `[`, turning the intended quote character-class into a literal `['"` sequence, and `core\.voice\[` presumes an identifier named `core` that no file in apps/ or packages/ uses for the voice namespace import.
attacks.evidence: S1 verification text (b) as written; parsing `\[` in rg yields a literal open-bracket, not a class; `rg -n 'core\.voice' apps packages -g '!node_modules'` returns nothing at baseline, so the command 'passes' regardless of reality — a fail-open guard.
attacks.repair: Specify the exact executable patterns: `rg -n "['\"](nearestPixelWithin|assertTriggerGraphIntegrity|listCanvasScenes)['\"]" -g '!node_modules' -g '!docs'` (quoted-name form covers obj['x'], obj["x"] and string-keyed maps), plus a backtick variant, each with its expected-empty output recorded in evidence-no-callers.md.

The finding's proposed_fix offers no caller either; graph-integrity.ts:218-223 has zero call sites including tests.
attacks.repair: On 'keep': record Trent's intent answer in the ledger, leave the function untouched, and file a follow-up ticket to wire the intended caller (graph-import/authoring validation path) — explicitly out of this initiative's scope. Delete the 'add a caller in the same change' clause.

attacks.evidence: packages/core/src/index.ts:33 (`export * from './canvas/registry'`) and :73 (`export * as voice from './voice'`) make all three symbols in-principle reachable via namespace objects; nothing in the test suite covers them (finding evidence: testfiles=0).
attacks.plan_response: S1 verification (b) rules out bracket/template-string access before any deletion, (c) runs knip's unused-export scan, and behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.known_gaps item (2) names exactly this gap for listCanvasScenes and designates the rg+knip output as the substitute evidence — the mechanism is right even though the literal regexes need the S1 repair above.

attacks.claim: Deleting barrel-reachable exports (listCanvasScenes via index.ts:33, assertTriggerGraphIntegrity via the voice namespace at index.ts:73) breaks external consumers of @ledrums/core that the plan never names.
